data.narrative:
Cresilon, a Series B biotech company founded by Joe Landolina, has raised $113M to date. Valuation is benchmarked against a universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage comparables in Biotech & Health, with particular weight on 3 same-sector Series C companies: Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $113M raised proxy, implying a $215M valuation at the next funding stage. Peer-median analysis across the three Series C comparables yields a $3.8B median valuation, with a range of $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring using a sector P/S median of 8.1x cannot be applied, as target revenue is not disclosed. The wide dispersion in peer multiples—notably Colossal Biosciences at $10.3B versus New Limit at $3.1B—reflects material variance in development stage, IP maturity, or clinical progress within the same cohort.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $182M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.0B. The gap between stage-progression ($215M) and peer-median ($3.8B) reflects Cresilon's earlier stage relative to the comparison set. Key uncertainties include clinical milestone completion, IP defensibility, and market adoption trajectory—factors that would justify positioning toward either pole of the peer range.
